answers.In a sentence or two, what will it do fo: It works through procurement tasks, decides its own steps, calls internal systems and places supplier orders without a checkpoint.
answers.Where does the AI come from?: Something a team in your firm built for this job
answers.What kind of AI is it?: An AI agent that works through tasks on its own, using other tools or systems — e.g. sends messages, books things, updates records, changes code
What information will it see or use?: Confidential firm information — internal data, code or documents not meant for outside the firm, whether or not they’re marked confidential
answers.What happens with what it produces?: acts entirely by itself, with no person involved at any point
answers.Which of these does it help decide, if a: None of these — it’s for day-to-day work
answers.How widely will it be used?: Just me, or a small trial
answers.What does it do when it acts?: Something else — sends, books, updates records, deploys changes
What can it get into by itself?: It has its own logins, passwords or access tokens for other systems

didntUnderstand: "Who ends up seeing or receiving what it produces" options: my tool sends orders to outside suppliers, and no option names suppliers or other outside businesses. I couldn't tell which one fits, so I chose Not sure.

"If it gets something wrong, can the mistake be caught and put right before it does lasting harm — to anyone?": it depends on whether a supplier order can be cancelled, which I don't know. I'm unsure what counts as lasting harm.
"What does it do when it acts?" has trades and yes-or-no decisions as the named options. My tool is neither, so "Something else" is a catch-all. I'm unsure why it matters which one I pick.
"It runs on computers or servers shared with other automated tools": I didn't tick it because I don't know my hosting setup. I also don't know why it matters.

The screens never say what the 'Similar checks' step does. The form also shows pre-fills for three other questions (information, recipients, countries) that don't match my tool, and my packet doesn't list them. I'd ignore them and answer my own way.
On the describe screen, "Make it smarter" and the Ollama setup text (signin, OLLAMA_ORIGINS) are unclear. I don't know what the model does, or whether I need to set it up.
expectNext: After Continue I expect the form to check that every required question is answered and every suggested answer has been confirmed. Then I'd get a Confirm screen where I can review everything, and then a Result. The Result should say whether I can go ahead, what is broken, and what controls I need first. Because my tool acts with no person involved and has its own logins, I expect it to be flagged as out of appetite or needing heavy controls. The result should come from the firm's written rules, not from AI.
ticksMean: "I've checked this answer" means I've read the model's suggestion, and the words it quoted from my description, and I agree with it. It's me confirming the guess, not the model deciding. Nothing is final until Confirm, and I can still change any answer. Unticked suggestions block Continue ("Still to check").
comment: I'd call this form clear for a developer, apart from the recipients question, which has no option for outside suppliers, and the unfamiliar approval jargon.
